summary: A change notice from BBN for a new IMP system version. It raised the number of hosts one IMP can serve from three to four, collected more detailed statistics on host use for the Network Control Center, and changed the time unit of one timing statistic. BBN expected no direct effect on hosts.

plainLanguage.summary: BBN announces three changes in IMP system version 2505. The IMP can handle another host, reports more host-use information and uses a different unit for a timing statistic.

questions: imp host limit raised to four
how many hosts could the imp handle
subtitle: A notice of capacity and statistics changes in IMP system version 2505.

tldr.problem: The IMP system needed to support another host and provide more complete host-usage statistics to the Network Control Center.
tldr.mechanism: Version 2505 raises the supported host count from three to four, changes statistics collection and adjusts the time unit for a round-trip statistic.
tldr.outcome: BBN expected no direct effect on hosts; external changes included an additional status light and longer statistics reports.

today: RFC 213 is an IMP system change notice published in August 1971. The unit metadata lists its status as Unknown.

sections.title: More Host Capacity
sections.content:
BBN installed IMP system version 2505 during the week of August 16. The system's host-handling capacity increased from three hosts to four.

The visible effects were a new status light, light 8, for Host 4, and longer 10-second and snapshot statistics.
sections.plainLanguage: The IMP can now handle four hosts instead of three. A new light shows Host 4, and some reports became longer.

sections.title: Host Usage Statistics
sections.content:
The host-handling routines were changed to collect more accurate and more extensive statistics about host use of the network and report them to the Network Control Center.

The host round-trip measurement in the 10-second statistics changed from units of 100 microseconds to units of 800 microseconds.
sections.plainLanguage: The IMP reports more information about host use to the Network Control Center. The round-trip statistic is now measured in units of 800 microseconds.

sections.title: Expected Host Impact
sections.content: The notice says BBN did not anticipate any direct effect on hosts from the new system version.
sections.plainLanguage: BBN expected host systems to continue working without a direct change.
